nominal_positions.interpretation: The implied masculine altar is built up to the knee in the first clause.
Navel level in the second building.
The Pada separates grīva from daghnam. The commentary explains the short final vowel of the first constituent.
The Gāyatrī as the means in the first ascent clause, written गायत्रिया in the Pada.
The second clause relates the Triṣṭubh to the midspace.
The third clause names the Jagatī as means.
The destination of the second ascent.
Depth in digging, agreeing with the feminine bed of the altar.
The explicit accusative object of the prior digging.
Thumb-sized. The bearer in this verse is puruṣaḥ.
The measured subject rather than a unit for a second entity.
Neuter cited measure with aṇ on puruṣa.
Neuter elephant measure with grade and retained stem n.
Moat of two-person measure, explicitly both feminine forms.
The same two choices on the three-person standard.
Frozen long-ī nominative of the two-elephant measurement, after inner luk.
Three-elephant measurement on the same n-final feminine route.
The previously noted palm term now has its explicit nominative position. PG782 had no case row for it.

source_policy_decisions.decision: Vertical extent selects dvayasac or daghnac while mātrac also allows a vessel quantity. The attached marker histories survive when known units undergo luk. PG755 owns the counted seers.
Preserve neck with the Taittirīya short a and the other two textual landmarks as separate source observations. Only the named Taittirīya commentator explicitly gives this rule history.

The human standard takes a separate measured bearer. At Kaṭha 2.1.12 the human is that bearer and the thumb supplies the standard. The optional human-unit and n-final elephant feminines have independent explanations.

An altar piled up and an altar bed dug down give distinct participants, gender and direction on the same knee standard. No new bare ci finite position is inferred from an independently attested token.
Keep the divided abhi of victory, the ordered preverbs of ascent, and their respective active third singulars. Each repeated world/height association receives one source-local analysis.
